sections.text:
1 Ex angelo Raziel scriptor factus est. Excerpta quaedam sub nomine Raziel
tradita sunt sed " Liber Institutionis " ab Alberto inspectus latine exstare non
videtur. Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 384 ss. et p. 396. De hebraicis versionibus,
cf. Die hebräischen Uebersetz., p. 937.
2 Liber de capite Saturni ignotus est. Conferendus est liber Saturni Hermetis
supra p. 101, et ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Κρόνου λεγόμενος qui graece laudatur, cf. supra
p. 52 (cod. 2, f. 247v).
3 De his libris Hermetis, qui periisse videntur, cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 373,
l, m. — Ἰατρομαθηματικά Hermetis graece edita sunt ab Idelero, cf. Catal., I, p. 61.
4 Hic liber aliunde ignotus esse videtur. Editionis Lugdunensis textus " liber
quem vocant Amorem animae vel potius Mortem animae " num alicuius sit momenti
nescio.
sections.en:
1 From the angel Raziel he was made a writer. Certain excerpts have been handed down under the name of Raziel but the "Liber Institutionis" inspected by Albert does not seem to exist in Latin. Cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 384 ff. and p. 396. On the Hebrew versions, cf. Die hebräischen Uebersetz., p. 937.
2 The Liber de capite Saturni is unknown. The liber Saturni of Hermes above p. 101 is to be compared, and the ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Κρόνου λεγόμενος which is praised in Greek, cf. above p. 52 (cod. 2, f. 247v).
3 On these books of Hermes, which seem to have perished, cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 373, l, m. — The Ἰατρομαθηματικά of Hermes were edited in Greek by Ideler, cf. Catal., I, p. 61.
4 This book seems to be unknown from elsewhere. Whether the text of the Lyon edition "liber quem vocant Amorem animae vel potius Mortem animae" is of any importance I do not know.

summary.headline: Hermetic and Magical Books
summary.text: Catalogue of astrological and magical books, including the fifteen secret names of Mahomet, Raziel’s Liber Institutionis, a book On the Head of Saturn, two natural works of Hermes on planetary medicines and animal-catching confections, Hermes to Aristotle, and Aristotle’s book to Alexander called the Death of the Soul. The closing list mentions images made with fumigations, invocations, exorcisms, and inscribed characters.
